note: Window agent m1800-m1701. The First Sealand dynasty keyframe -1732 used a box (42-50 E, 27-32.3 N) for Sumer that swallowed the Saudi desert, Kuwait and the Gulf (1,477 cells in the draft); replaced by the Cliopatria marsh shape plus the Dhi-Qar and Basra governorates and Uruk (the page's pottery evidence). Nippur and Isin follow by event in -1721 (Samsu-iluna's year 29, when their records stop). Reviewer (2 Nov): events/1 and keyframe_overrides/1 keep Nippur, Isin and southern Akkad Babylonian for -1732..-1722 (the narrowed Sealand keyframe had left them nobody's); events/0 now takes them from babylonia.

region.text: Nippur and Isin, whose records 'keep going ... until Samsu-iluna's 29th year, and then cease'; Nippur 'recognized Ilum-ma-ili as king' by Samsu-iluna's death

events.note: c. 1721 BC: the northern Sumerian cities pass to Ilum-ma-ili. Samsu-iluna page: 'Records keep going in Nippur and Isin until Samsu-iluna's 29th year, and then cease there as well' and 'by the time of Samsu-iluna's death, Nippur recognized Ilum-ma-ili as king'; Sealand page: he 'is thought to have conquered Nippur late in Samsu-iluna's reign'. Year 29 = 1721 BC in the dating the dossier uses (years 18-29 = 1732-1721). Babylonia holds these cells to this year by events/1 and keyframe_overrides/1 (reviewer, 2 Nov), so the counterpart is babylonia. Restores the Nippur land the old box gave the Sealand from -1732.

region.text: Nippur, Isin and Akkad, which Samsu-iluna kept until his year 29: 'Records keep going in Nippur and Isin until Samsu-iluna's 29th year'

events.note: c. 1732-1721 BC: Nippur and Isin stay with Babylon while the far south secedes. Samsu-iluna page: 'in the 18th year of his reign, he saw to the rebuilding of 6 fortresses in the vicinity of Nippur' and 'Records keep going in Nippur and Isin until Samsu-iluna's 29th year, and then cease there as well' (year 18 = 1732, year 29 = 1721; reign 1749-1712 BC, middle chronology). Added by the reviewer: Babylonia's loss (ledger/7) and the Sealand's found (ledger/0) use a box that reaches 32.3 N and takes Nippur, Isin and the south of Akkad; with the Sealand's -1732 keyframe narrowed (keyframe_overrides/0) these cells were left nobody's until events/0 in -1721. This event keeps them Babylonian; events/0 passes Nippur and Isin to the Sealand in -1721.

correction.text: the marsh core at the head of the Gulf plus the Dhi-Qar and Basra governorates (Girsu, Lagash, Ur, Larsa) and Uruk: 'Sealand pottery has been found at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that'

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's keyframe adds a polygon 42-50 E, 27-32.3 N: 1,320 cells of Saudi desert, Kuwait and the Gulf that no page assigns to the Sealand. The Sealand page names a province 'in the far south of Mesopotamia' and finds Sealand pottery 'at Girsu, Uruk, and Lagash but in no site north of that'; the Samsu-iluna page has Uruk, Ur and Kisurra among the rebel cities. Nippur and Isin are added by event in -1721. The -1700, -1600 and -1500 keyframes of the dossier carry the same polygon (they start in later windows).

union.text: the Euphrates up to and including the ruins of Mari

correction.text: Akkad and the Euphrates to Mari, with Nippur and Isin (held to Samsu-iluna's year 29, 1721)

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's -1732 keyframe (Akkad and the Euphrates to Mari) leaves out Nippur and Isin, which the Samsu-iluna page keeps Babylonian until his 29th year ('Records keep going in Nippur and Isin until Samsu-iluna's 29th year, and then cease there as well'; fortresses rebuilt 'in the vicinity of Nippur' in year 18). Added by the reviewer with events/1 so that the -1732 snap keeps them; events/0 passes them to the Sealand in -1721. The keyframe is compared only in -1732, so it does not pull them back after -1721.
